title: Invertibility of the intrinsic compact scalar transpose on bounded constructible input
statement: Let A and B be finite commutative rings, phi:A -> B a ring homomorphism, and c=(j,p) a compactification [def-weil-compactifications-refinements] of f:X -> Y with c.Z and Y Noetherian. Define the intrinsic scalar mate as the scalar-adjunction transpose of the specified compact-support restriction comparison [def-finite-compact-scalar-transport-data]. If K in D(X_proet,A) [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules] has intrinsically constructible cohomology [def-weil-proetale-constructible-sheaf] supported in finitely many degrees, and K tensor_A^L B has cohomology supported in finitely many degrees, then this intrinsic scalar mate at K is invertible. No constructibility of the scalar extension and no flatness of phi are assumed.

proof.text: Finite cohomological support has a lower and an upper bound, also when it is empty. Apply the finite-ring essential-image criterion to choose a bounded constructible etale antecedent G and its intrinsic realization isomorphism eG to K. The antecedent is used only up to that isomorphism.

source.place: Compact-support and final paragraphs; normalized scalar isomorphisms proof steps 2, 3, 4

proof.text: Let GB be the actual etale derived scalar extension of G. The specified siteScalarIso followed by scalar extension of eG identifies the intrinsic realization of GB with the scalar extension of K. Transport a cohomological interval along this isomorphism and reflect it using the interval equivalence of the finite-ring comparison theorem. Thus GB is bounded below, and G already is bounded below.

source.place: Compact-support and final paragraphs; normalized scalar isomorphisms proof steps 2, 3, 4

proof.text: Expand the scalar transpose using its unit equation. Apply intrinsicCompactScalarIsoOfOrigin_hom with G and GB regarded as D+ objects and the identity scalar comparison. Its right side is the hom of an explicitly constructed isomorphism, so the intrinsic scalar mate at the realization of G is invertible.

proof.text: Naturality at eG identifies the mate at K, composed with the scalar compact-support image of eG, with the known invertible mate followed by compact support of scalar extension of eG. These other factors are isomorphisms. Cancel them to obtain invertibility at K.
